## Controls in detail

### A01 — Broken Access Control

**Required control (§8.1):** Role-based access checks on every endpoint; tests verify unauthorised access returns 403.

**How the application implements it:** `middleware/auth.js` provides `protect` (valid token, live and active account) and `authorize(...roles)`. Every non-public route composes them. Resource-scoped lookups (payments, invoices, certificates) filter by the caller’s own id.

**Assessment:** Every one of the 82 admin-only endpoints is probed anonymously and with a student token on every CI run, driven from the generated endpoint inventory so a new route is covered automatically. The open gap is self-registration: the public registration endpoint accepts a client-supplied `role`, so anyone can create an administrator (DEFECT-11).

### A02 — Cryptographic Failures

**Required control (§8.1):** Passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost factor ≥ 12); tokens stored as hashes; TLS enforced.

**How the application implements it:** Passwords are hashed by a `pre("save")` hook and the field is `select: false`. Reset tokens are returned raw to the caller and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. Strict-Transport-Security is set in production.

**Assessment:** Hashing, storage and non-disclosure are all verified. The cost factor is 10, not the 12 the course requires (DEFECT-02) — a one-character change in `models/User.js`.

**Evidence:**

### A03 — Injection

**Required control (§8.1):** Parameterised queries or ORM used throughout; input validated and sanitised.

**How the application implements it:** Mongoose casts every query against its schema, and `strict` mode drops unknown paths. express-validator guards each write endpoint. A global regular-expression filter is also installed in `server.js`.

**Assessment:** Operator-injection attempts against login, path parameters and the registration body are all rejected — the ORM is doing the work. The global filter, however, is mounted before `express.json()` and never inspects a request body at all (DEFECT-30), while on query strings it rejects ordinary words such as "and" and "or" (DEFECT-01). The course search interpolates the raw term into `$regex` (DEFECT-16).

**Evidence:**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `TC-SEC-A03-03` | Registration cannot inject fields the schema does not declare | Security | ✅ Pass |
| `TC-SEC-A03-04` | A script payload in a profile field is stored and returned as plain text | Security | ✅ Pass |
| `TC-SEC-A03-05` | A query string containing SQL keywords is rejected | Security | ✅ Pass |
| `TC-SEC-A03-06` | A legitimate search term is not rejected as an attack | Security | ⚠️ documents DEFECT-01 |
| `TC-NFR-04-U01` | handleValidationErrors continues when no rule failed | Unit | ✅ Pass |

### A04 — Insecure Design

**Required control (§8.1):** Threat model documented in the SDS Security section; design reviewed against it.

**How the application implements it:** Rate limiting over the whole API surface, upload type and size restrictions, business-rule guards (no duplicate enrolment, no double completion, no refund of an uncollected payment) enforced in both the application and the database.

**Assessment:** The rate limiter is proven to fire, and the business-rule guards hold. Two design gaps remain: a refund is never compared against the original amount (DEFECT-22), and a single global limit covers browsing and password guessing alike (DEFECT-32). The threat model itself belongs in the SDS and is outside this repository.

### A05 — Security Misconfiguration

**Required control (§8.1):** Default credentials removed; error messages do not leak stack traces in production.

**How the application implements it:** helmet plus explicit X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and a Content-Security- Policy; X-Powered-By removed; a generic error handler that discloses `error.message` only outside production; CORS restricted to configured origins.

**Assessment:** Headers, error hygiene and the absence of committed credentials are all verified, including that the unauthenticated health endpoint never echoes the database URI. The open gap is the hard-coded `fallback-secret` used for JWT signing whenever JWT_SECRET is unset (DEFECT-03) — a deployment that forgets one variable is trivially forgeable.

| `TC-SEC-A05-04` | The application refuses to start without an explicit JWT secret | Security | ⚠️ documents DEFECT-03 |
| `TC-NFR-03-11` | The health probe does not disclose the database connection string | Integration | ✅ Pass |
| `TC-NFR-03-12` | Every response carries the baseline security headers | Integration | ✅ Pass |

### A06 — Vulnerable and Outdated Components

**Required control (§8.1):** Dependency scan in the CI pipeline; no high or critical vulnerabilities.

**How the application implements it:** `npm audit --audit-level=high` runs on every push in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, against both the test repository and the application. Dependabot is configured in the application repository.

**Assessment:** Enforced by the pipeline rather than by a test case: the check is about the dependency tree at a point in time, and the audit job fails the build on a high or critical advisory. The current result is attached to each CI run.

**Evidence:** enforced by the CI pipeline; see the linked workflow run.

### A07 — Identification and Authentication Failures

**Required control (§8.1):** Account lockout after N failed attempts; secure session management; MFA optional.

**How the application implements it:** A password complexity policy at registration, bcrypt verification, deactivated-account refusal, bounded token lifetime, and an HTTP-only session cookie that is `secure` in production.

**Assessment:** Weak passwords are rejected, credentials are verified correctly, and the failure message is identical for an unknown account and a wrong password, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate users. Three gaps: no account lockout (DEFECT-31), logout does not invalidate the token server-side (DEFECT-14), and the change-password endpoint does not apply the registration policy (DEFECT-20).

| `TC-SEC-A07-03` | The session cookie is HTTP-only, so script cannot read it | Security | ✅ Pass |

### A08 — Software and Data Integrity Failures

**Required control (§8.1):** Package lock files committed; the pipeline verifies integrity.

**How the application implements it:** `package-lock.json` is committed in both repositories and CI installs with `npm ci`, which refuses to proceed if the lockfile and manifest disagree.

**Assessment:** Enforced by the pipeline. `npm ci` verifies the integrity hash of every package against the lockfile, so a tampered or drifted dependency fails the build before any test runs.

**Evidence:** enforced by the CI pipeline; see the linked workflow run.

### A09 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

**Required control (§8.1):** All auth events, errors and data access logged; logs do not contain PII or secrets.

**How the application implements it:** morgan logs every request; `server.js` adds explicit audit lines for authentication successes and failures and for every administrative action, naming the acting user.

**Assessment:** The audit trail itself is present and covers the events the course requires. The content is the problem: `middleware/auth.js` prints the JWT signing secret and a token prefix on every authenticated request (DEFECT-05), and validation errors echo the submitted password back to the client (DEFECT-13). Both are one-line removals.

**Evidence:**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TC-SEC-A09-01` | No application log statement prints a secret | Security | ⚠️ documents DEFECT-05 |
| `TC-SEC-A09-02` | Authentication outcomes are logged for audit | Security | ✅ Pass |
| `TC-NFR-03-02` | A validation error does not echo the submitted password back to the client | Integration | ⚠️ documents DEFECT-13 |

**Open defects:** DEFECT-05, DEFECT-13

### A10 — Server-Side Request Forgery

**Required control (§8.1):** External URL inputs validated; allow-list of permitted domains.

**How the application implements it:** The only user-supplied URL is the profile `website` field. No route dereferences it, so there is no server-side fetch to forge.

**Assessment:** Verified that no route makes an outbound request from a user-supplied URL, which means classic SSRF is not reachable. The field is nonetheless unvalidated beyond its length (DEFECT-06): `javascript:`, `file://` and link-local addresses are all stored and later rendered as a link, so the live risk is stored-XSS and phishing rather than SSRF.

**Evidence:**

| Test case | Description | Layer | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TC-SEC-A10-01` | A user-supplied website URL is validated against an allow-list | Security | ⚠️ documents DEFECT-06 |

**Open defects:** DEFECT-06
